title: The data entry form: its panels and boxes
one: Five panels, two buttons, and a name on every control.

next.title: Global.cs: the file that remembers things between forms

stages.title: Check what your data entry form has
stages.thing: your data entry form so far

screens.title: Check what your data entry form already has
screens.done: every row is ticked, or you have gone where its link says
screens.goal: I check my data entry form for its five panels, their names, the Save and View Report buttons and the year group list.

blocks.p: Your data entry form may be partly made already.
This screen checks what is there.

check.what: Open frmDataEntry in the Design tab. Does it have five panels?
check.how: They hold the pupil details, three attempts, the quiz, the reaction test and the group.

check.what: Click the edge of each panel once. In Properties, does its Name start with pnl?
check.how: The Name line is near the top of Properties.

check.what: Under the panels, are there two big buttons, Save Details and View Report?
check.how: They sit on the form itself, outside the five panels.

check.what: Click the year group list once. In Properties, click Items. Are the year groups in it?
check.how: Items opens a box with one choice on each line.

screens.title: See the five panels, then make them
screens.goal: This part shows the five panels of the data entry form, then you drag them on and name them.

open.what: The data entry form is where a user types in one pupil. Five panels split it into five jobs.
open.does: When it works, your data entry form has five named panels. Each name starts with pnl.

screens.title: See the five panels on the data entry form
screens.done: you can name the five panels and say what each one holds
screens.goal: The data entry form holds five panels: pupil details, three attempts, the quiz, the reaction test and the group.

blocks.p: The data entry form is where a user types in one pupil.
It holds five panels.

flow.watch: Count the five panels and read each one's name
flow.say: Five panels: pupil details, attempts, quiz, test and group.

blocks.p: Each panel holds the controls for one job. The Save and View Report buttons sit under them.

blocks.yours: In MY example the second panel holds three swim lengths. YOURS holds whatever YOUR task measures three times. Name the panel for what it holds.

screens.title: Put on the five panels and name each one
screens.done: five panels sit on your form, each named with pnl at the start
screens.goal: I drag five panels onto the data entry form and give each one a name that starts with pnl.

blocks.p: Make the panels first.
The boxes and buttons go inside them on the next screens.

steps.do: In Solution Explorer, double-click frmDataEntry. It opens in the Design tab.
steps.see: The data entry form, empty or partly made.

steps.do: Drag a Panel from the Toolbox onto the form. The Toolbox is down the left side. Drag the corner to make it bigger.
steps.see: A box with a dotted edge sits on the form.

steps.do: Click the panel's edge once. In Properties, find the word Name. Type its new name and press Enter.
steps.see: The Name line shows the new name, like pnlPupilDetails.
wrong: Clicking the middle picks the wrong thing.
Click the dotted EDGE of the panel, not the middle.

steps.do: Do the same for the other four panels.
steps.see: Five panels, each with a name that starts with pnl.

frames.alt: A control on the form clicked once, with its handles showing
frames.say: Click the control once. Little squares appear round it.

frames.alt: The Properties window with the Name line near the top
frames.say: In Properties, find the word Name. It is near the top of the list.

frames.alt: The Name line in Properties changed to a new name
frames.say: Type the new name and press Enter.

blocks.watch: MY panel names are pnlPupilDetails, pnlSwimLengths, pnlQuizResult, pnlReactionTest and pnlSwimmingGroup. Name YOURS for what they hold.

stages.title: Inside each panel
stages.thing: the boxes and buttons in each panel

screens.title: Fill each panel with its boxes and buttons
screens.goal: This part puts the right controls inside each of the five panels, one panel per screen.

open.what: Each panel gets its own labels, boxes, lists and buttons. One screen does one panel, from a table.
open.does: When it works, every panel holds its controls. The two big buttons sit under the panels.

screens.title: Fill the pupil details panel
screens.done: every row of the table sits inside the pupil details panel
screens.goal: The pupil details panel holds a first name box, a surname box, a gender list, a year group list, an Enter button and a ? button.

blocks.p: The first panel holds the pupil's name, gender and year group.
Drag each row INSIDE pnlPupilDetails.
A ComboBox is a drop-down list that the user picks from.

controls.done: Two boxes, two drop-down lists, their labels and two buttons sit inside the pupil details panel.

screens.title: Put the choices in the two drop-down lists
screens.done: both drop-down lists hold their choices, one per line
screens.goal: The year group list and the gender list each hold their choices, typed one per line in Items.

blocks.p: A drop-down list is empty until you give it its choices.
They go in [[Items|0]], one per line.

words: The choices in a drop-down list, one on each line.
blocks.intro: One new thing in this chapter. Click the marked word to see what it means.

steps.do: In the Design tab, click the year group list once.
steps.see: Little squares appear round the year group list.

steps.do: In Properties, find Items. Click the three dots beside it.
steps.see: A box opens for typing the choices.

steps.do: Type one choice on each line. Then click OK.
wrong: All my choices show on one line.
Press Enter after each choice, so each one has its own line.

steps.do: Do the same for the gender list.
steps.see: Both lists now hold their choices.

blocks.watch: MY year group list holds 11 to 14. YOURS holds the choices YOUR task sheet gives you.

screens.title: Fill the three attempts panel
screens.done: every row of the table sits inside the three attempts panel
screens.goal: The second panel holds three attempt boxes with labels, a Calculate Average button, a box for the average and a ? button.

blocks.p: The second panel holds three attempts and their average.
Drag each row INSIDE pnlSwimLengths.

controls.done: Three attempt boxes, the average box and two buttons sit inside the second panel.

blocks.p: The Calculate Average button does nothing yet. You make it work in chapter 5.

screens.title: Fill the quiz panel and the reaction test panel
screens.done: the first four rows sit in the quiz panel and the last four in the test panel
screens.goal: The quiz panel and the test panel each hold a heading, a not taken yet label, a Take button and a ? button.

blocks.p: These two panels look alike.
Each one has a heading, a line that says not taken yet, and two buttons.

controls.done: The first four rows sit inside pnlQuizResult. The last four sit inside pnlReactionTest.

blocks.watch: The first four rows go in the QUIZ panel. The last four go in the TEST panel.

screens.title: Fill the group panel and add the two big buttons
screens.done: the group panel is filled and the two big buttons sit on the form
screens.goal: The group panel holds a heading, a box, a button and a ? button. Save Details, View Report, a title and a logo sit on the form.

blocks.p: The first four rows go INSIDE pnlSwimmingGroup, and the rest sit on the form.
A PictureBox shows a picture. StretchImage makes the picture fill the whole box.

controls.done: Four rows sit inside the group panel. Two big buttons, the title and the logo sit on the form.

blocks.p: For Image, click its three dots, then Import, then YOUR logo file.

blocks.watch: Every ? button's name starts btnHelp. They all start working in chapter 13.

stages.title: Try it in the Design tab

screens.title: Check every name on your data entry form
screens.done: every row is ticked, or you have gone where its link says
screens.goal: Every panel name starts pnl, every text box tbx, every button btn and every drop-down list cbx. None is a made-up name.

blocks.p: A wrong name stops your code finding a control later.
Click each control once and read its Name.

check.what: Every panel's name starts with pnl.
check.how: Click the dotted edge of each panel once.

check.what: Every text box's name starts with tbx.
Every button's name starts with btn, and every drop-down list's name starts with cbx.
check.how: Click each button and each list once.

check.what: Click any control once and read its Name.
check.how: It must NOT be a made-up name like textBox1 or panel3.
check.fix: Give it a real name, as on part 2, screen 2.
